parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the need for a pure Node.js ESM, zero-dependency reimplementation of Python-Markdown behavior, argparse-compatible --a through --f handling, phase ordering, tables, fenced code, codehilite, and toc output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It chose a two-stage plan: five spec/probing children first, then a contract, then a separate coder swarm with ENGINE, HL1, HL2, and CLI roles. Ownership existed but productive implementation was deferred.
parallel.implementation: The only delivered implementation pieces were the CLI entry point and argparse support; the markdown engine and highlighter modules were still unfinished when the implementation swarm was aborted.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivery was not a coherent task solution: artifact validation copied only test19.mjs, CONTRACT.md, and lib/argparse.mjs, so imports required by the entry path were absent.
parallel.verification: The first phase gathered specs and the CLI child tested argparse/mock wiring, but no completed whole-task markdown differential or official-aligned integrated verification occurred before closure.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Core markdown conversion, extension processing, Pygments/codehilite behavior, and end-to-end integration were missing from the final artifact; official evaluation passed 0 of 70.

serial.requirements: The serial run worked from the same prompt and recognized manual argparse compatibility, phased markdown conversion, tables/fenced-code/codehilite/toc behavior, ESM modules, and no external dependencies.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It kept all work in the main trajectory: probe executable behavior, implement parser/highlighter/CLI files directly, run local differential checks, and adjust observed failures.
serial.implementation: It wrote a partial but broad implementation tree including test19.mjs, inline/html stash/extensions/blocks modules, and multiple pygments-style highlighter modules.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact contained a coherent entry plus supporting libraries, so the evaluator could execute real markdown behavior even though the implementation was incomplete.
serial.verification: It ran sample differential checks: test1 passed, test2 passed, test3 exposed diffs in HTML escaping and Python tokenization, and test4 passed before cancellation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial implementation still missed harder markdown/highlighting details and timed out after partial fixes, leading to official failure despite 15 of 70 samples passing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the same conversion requirements and recorded them in a contract after reading the prompt and first-wave specs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and implemented around the required phases, arguments, ESM layout, and markdown extensions.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was not the main difference; parallel failed to deliver core recognized requirements, while serial implemented enough recognized behavior to pass simple cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work into a spec-only first swarm and then four implementation roles, making implementation dependent on a later stage.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no subagents and kept implementation, integration, and tests in one main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's decomposition delayed production work behind a research phase; serial began producing and testing implementation artifacts directly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created CONTRACT.md to share interfaces and gave coder roles explicit scope, so missing context was not the direct failure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained all task context locally and did not need cross-agent handoffs or interface reconciliation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The cross-agent context mechanism was present in parallel, but the later implementers did not survive to deliver against it; serial avoided that coordination boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel landed only CLI/argparse-related files in the final artifact and lacked the imported markdown/highlight implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a multi-file partial markdown/highlighting implementation with an executable entry point.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel essentially delivered only scaffolding; serial delivered a runnable partial implementation that passed some evaluator cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel's active coder swarm returned as aborted, with children canceled before final implementation results were complete.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its main trajectory accumulated local changes until the run timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost in-progress child work at the lifecycle boundary, while serial kept partial work in the final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel's final copied tree contained test19.mjs, CONTRACT.md, and argparse only, so integrated imports for markdown/highlighting were absent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial's final tree contained the entry file plus inline, block, extension, htmlStash, and pygments-style modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did not assemble a coherent final implementation, whereas serial assembled an incomplete but integrated library tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had no successful end-to-end acceptance evidence and official evaluation reported zero passed samples.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local differential samples, passed tests 1, 2, and 4, exposed a diff in test3, and official evaluation passed 15 samples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closed without integrated verification; serial used local sample feedback and retained a partially verified implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the run budget with spec work, retry overhead, and active coder children that were aborted at closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but most budget went into direct implementation and sample-based debugging before cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both timed out, but parallel's budget left the final deliverable structurally incomplete, while serial's budget produced a partial solution with measurable coverage.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official relation is both_fail, not a discordant pass/fail outcome. The material quality gap is that parallel delivered only scaffolding after a spec-first multi-agent plan and an aborted coder swarm, while serial delivered a coherent partial implementation tree and passed 15 of 70 tests.
parallel_contributors: A standalone first-phase investigation deferred productive implementation until after CONTRACT.md was written.
The subsequent implementation swarm was explicitly aborted while ENGINE/HL children were still active.
The delivered artifact lacked core markdown and highlighter modules, leaving test19.mjs unable to represent the requested full pipeline.
serial_contributors: The serial main trajectory directly wrote a multi-file markdown/highlighting implementation instead of waiting for child handoffs.
It ran sample differential tests and preserved a partial implementation that passed 15 official samples.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial still had ordinary implementation mismatches in complex fenced-code, HTML escaping, and highlighting behavior, as shown by the sample 3 diff.
Parallel did not reach enough core implementation for ordinary markdown algorithm defects to dominate the final result.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No official pass/fail discordance; these are supported comparative contributors to the parallel quality deficit, not an exclusive root cause.
